evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Too lumpy today?' is a question, but the lede directly under it says it reads tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach and shows the swim windows. 'iPhone' appears only in the grey note beside the button, not in the lede.
evidence.fit: The brief's 'never tell anyone it is safe' rule gets its own band ('Conditions, not permission') and a footer line, and the page never uses the word safe. The colours move from night to grey morning section by section, which matches 'the sea at 6 am'. Every CTA goes to the supplied https://tidewise.example/beta.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero is a tide curve that bleeds off the page edge, with a hatched 'lost to the wind' band and a lock-screen notification mock. The middle of the page is still a conventional run of headline-and-prose bands, and the 'What it reads' section is a 2x2 definition list.
evidence.proof: The tide chart is operable in the hero: the range and a pointer drag update the status and the four values. At 1440x900 the readout (status at y~1050) and the caption 'A made-up November morning... Not a forecast' sit below the fold. At 390 the status starts at y=805 of 844. The numbers are consistent: 06:20 to 08:00 in the chart, the beach row and the notification, and 'last night 09:10' in both chart and notification.
evidence.craft: Inline CSS with tokens on :root and no external requests. axe: color-contrast 4.44:1 on the '.me' chat bubble (#dbe5e6 on #4d6b77), no <main> landmark, and 8-9 'region' violations. Cursor pill clipped at the edges: Home puts #cursorTime at left -26px and End puts its right edge at 1466px in a 1440 viewport; the hero has overflow:hidden, so half the pill is cut off. The chart spans the full viewport while the range sits inside .wrap (194-1250px at 1440), so the slider thumb does not line up with the cursor line. With JavaScript off, the chart paths are empty and the 'swim window' and 'lost to the wind' labels stack on top of each other at x=0.
evidence.mobile: No overflow at 390 or 320, and the smallest text is 12px. Targets under 44px: the range input is 28px tall, the header 'Join the beta' link is 40px and the logo link is 28px. At 390 the '.lost-label' is hidden, so the early-close band has no text label. After tapping the chart at 60% (08:05), the status update is at y=805-879, half below the 844 fold, so the feedback is not where the finger is.
evidence.honesty: Labels exist ('A made-up November morning at an example beach... Not a forecast', 'Example beaches and times.'). The hero chart's '06:20 to 08:00 swim window' and '06:10 now' are visible at 1440 with no example label in view; the label sits under the readout, below the first screen. The CTA says 'Join the public beta' and goes to the supplied URL.
evidence.interaction: Keyboard: Tab goes logo, 'Join the beta', CTA, range, final CTA, with a 2px #ebd6a8 outline on each and no skip link. Range Home/End/PageUp/arrows run through all four states: before ('Window opens at 06:20'), in ('In the window until 08:00 (1 h 40 min)'), early ('Window closed early at 08:00. Last night it ran to 09:10') and after. Mouse drag and touch tap on the chart work and clamp to 04:30 when dragged past the left edge. There is no reset control, aria-valuetext gives only the time, not the state, and there are no console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific, British and in the swimmer's own world: 'Four tabs and a group chat, at half five', 'Which gloves?', 'You look at the sea, and you decide.' Microcopy is written rather than defaulted ('Drag through the morning'). The header link 'Join the beta' and the CTA 'Join the public beta' differ slightly.
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: the H1, lede, CTA and top of the chart with '06:20 to 08:00 swim window' and '08:00 to 09:10 lost to the wind' are in view. The readout and the example caption are not, so the artifact that makes the promise believable is half shown and unlabelled. 390x844: the H1, lede, CTA and chart are in view, the status line is cut at the fold, and no example label is visible.

problems: The hero artifact's readout and its 'made-up morning, not a forecast' label sit below the first screen at 1440 and 390, and at 390 tap feedback lands half below the fold.

Robustness gaps: the cursor pill is half clipped at Home/End, the full-bleed chart does not line up with the in-wrap slider, there is no reset, and with JS off the chart is empty with overlapping labels.
Accessibility basics: no <main> landmark or skip link, axe contrast failure on the chat bubble (4.44:1), range and header link under 44px, and aria-valuetext without state.

evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Too lumpy today?' with the lede beside it: 'Tidewise is an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year. It reads the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach and shows today's swim windows.' The note under the CTA says 'iPhone public beta. 40 UK and Ireland beaches so far.' What, who and the next step are all on the first screen.
evidence.fit: The 'never safe' constraint is built into the artifact. The readout foot says 'Conditions only. Tidewise never tells you it's safe to swim', the 'Your call' section has 'You won't see: Safe to swim', and the readout states are worded 'In a window' and 'Outside the windows' rather than safe or unsafe. The early-close warning, which the brief names, is shown in the hero chart, the lanes and the warning card. All CTAs go to the supplied URL.
evidence.distinctiveness: A sea-surface chart whose chop is computed from swell plus onshore wind, a night-to-day sky band, and sample lanes that rebuild for the chosen morning. The structure is still a familiar sticky nav, hero and bands, and the visual weight is close to a data-dashboard look.
evidence.proof: At 1440x900 the operable chart, three scenario buttons, slider and readout are all in the first screen. The 'Sample mornings at an imaginary cove / Written for this page, not a forecast' label sits directly above the chart. The numbers agree across chart, readout, lanes, ledger ('W 8 mph, then NE 15-19 mph') and warning card ('07:42, not 09:30', '15 mph by 07:45'), because one tide.js generates them.
evidence.craft: axe (wcag2a/aa plus best-practice) reports 0 violations at all four widths. The page has a skip link, <main>, labelled navs, CSS tokens for colour, type and spacing, and reduced-motion handled in CSS. A build script (src/build.mjs) pre-renders the default state into the HTML, so with JS off the chart, readout and lanes still show and the menu falls back to inline links. Total loaded weight is about 76KB with no web fonts. Minor issues: the generated SVG path is about 15KB of duplicated inline markup, the you-dot is half clipped at 13:00 by the frame's overflow:hidden, and the readout re-renders its whole innerHTML inside role=status on every slider step, which makes screen readers chatty.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed. The H1 is on one line, the CTA sits at y~280, the scenario buttons and chart fit in the first screen, the extra labels (high water, first light, hint) are hidden, and alternate axis ticks are dropped. Every interactive element is 44px or taller. Menu: it opens as a 221px overlay, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button, and an outside click, tabbing out or tapping a link all close it. No overflow at 390 or 320. The readout starts at about y=790, so only its first line is in view under the slider.
evidence.honesty: Each example is labelled where it appears: the hero ('Written for this page, not a forecast'), the legend ('2.2 m tide limit (sample)'), 'Sample line, written for this page.' and 'Sample warning, written for this page'. Fail reasons in the readout say 'sample limit'. The bottom CTA note says 'Opens the beta page at tidewise.example/beta.' There are no reviews or numbers beyond the brief.
evidence.interaction: Keyboard: Tab runs skip link, brand, nav, CTA, Calm, 'Wind turns onshore', 'Big swell', slider, 'Reset the sample', with a 3px #f2c194 outline everywhere. The scenario buttons use aria-pressed. Slider Home/End and click both work. Edge states are handled: Big swell at 13:00 gives 'No window between 05:00 and 13:00' plus reasons ('Swell 1.4 m is over the 0.7 m sample limit...'). Calm at 05:00 gives 'Next window opens at 05:46, in 46 min'. Onshore at 08:20 gives 'The last one closed at 07:42, early: last night it ran to 09:30'. Reset returns to onshore at 06:30, focus stays on the button, and the lanes title resets. aria-valuetext includes the state. No console or page errors.
evidence.copy: Plain and specific: 'When you'd get in', 'Closes 07:42, not 09:30 / Wind turns onshore', 'Tidewise shows the water. Getting in is your call.' Terms stay consistent ('window', 'closes early'). The section H2 'Three websites, a tide table and the group chat become one line' is slightly clunky, and some lines repeat the not-a-lifeguard point.
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: the promise, the iPhone audience, the CTA and a labelled, operable sample with its readout ('06:30 In a window, 05:16-07:42 / Closes in 1 h 12 min. Closes early: last night it ran to 09:30') are all in one viewport. 390x844: the H1, lede, CTA, sample label, scenario buttons, chart and slider are in view, and the readout begins at the fold.

problems: The readout's live region rewrites its full contents on every 5-minute slider step, so screen readers will announce too much.
At 390 the readout sits under the chart and slider and starts at the fold, so most of the feedback needs a scroll.
The generated, duplicated ~15KB inline SVG path and the you-dot clipped at the 13:00 edge are small maintainability and visual blemishes.

reason: B is the more robust and maintainable page. It passes axe with 0 violations, every target is 44px or more, it has a skip link and landmarks, its menu handles Escape, outside click and focusout, it pre-renders a no-JS state, and the sample artifact handles every edge state with stated reasons and a reset, all labelled where it appears. A is well written, but its artifact feedback and example label fall below the fold, the cursor pill clips at the edges, it has no reset and no main landmark, and it renders an empty chart without JS. A showing that B's live-region chatter or generated markup broke something real for assistive tech would narrow the gap but not reverse it.
